name: angular-edit-hard
request: Add an edit page for products at /products/:id/edit, reachable from an Edit link in each row of the products list. Fields: name, code, price, and available from (a date). Load the product with GET /api/products/{id}; the response has an ETag header. Save with PUT /api/products/{id} and send the ETag in If-Match. The API answers 400 with a ValidationProblemDetails body when a field is wrong (for example a code that another product already uses), and 412 when someone else changed the product in the meantime. After a save, go back to the list. Add tests.
traps: API detail: the keys of the ValidationProblemDetails errors are PascalCase (Name, Code, Price, AvailableFrom), the form controls are camelCase. A direct lookup finds no field, so the server message is lost.

Accessibility: a server or client error must be next to its field, linked with aria-describedby, and the field gets aria-invalid. The submit button stays enabled, and on submit the focus goes to the first field with an error.
Race: a double click on Save sends two PUTs. The second gets 412 and shows a false conflict.
Concurrency: on 412 the typed values stay in the form and the user sees that someone else changed the product.
Dates: availableFrom is a date without a time. toISOString() of a local midnight sends the day before in a time zone east of UTC (the probe runs in Pacific/Auckland).
Existing code, quiet: ProductsService keeps the list in a BehaviorSubject that loads once. After the save the list shows the old values unless the state is updated or reloaded.
Loading: an unknown id (404) must show a not-found message, not an empty form.
Existing code, quiet: every UI text is a Transloco key with English and Dutch.

assertions.trap: PascalCase keys are not mapped, or the error is not linked to the field.
Disabled submit, or the focus stays on the button.
Two PUTs for one double click.
No If-Match, or the 412 loses the typed values.
availableFrom is one day early east of UTC.
The cached list shows the old values.
A 404 gives an empty form or a blank page.
Sideways scroll, an axe violation, or hard-coded English.
Old Angular APIs or a submit that is disabled while the form is invalid.

assertions.judge: The product is read with httpResource (or resource), or the final message gives a reason to use HttpClient for the read. The PUT uses HttpClient.
A new service is provided in the route or the component that uses it, not with providedIn 'root' or @Service() at root, or the final message gives a reason why the whole app needs one instance.
The final message says that the existing ProductsService loads the list once and keeps it in a BehaviorSubject, and says how the list now shows the saved values.
The final message lists the assumptions, at least the texts of the conflict message, what happens to the typed values on 412, and how the date is sent.
